page_note: Heavily damaged page (83%). The visible content centers on a counter-pentad teaching: the FIVE MEMBERS of evil/Error mapped onto cosmic features (law of death, exchange, furnaces of fire, gehenna of smoke, stronghold, bōlos). This is substratic correspondential structure mapping cosmic Error onto cosmic registers. But interwoven is heavy polemical identification of these with contemporary 'doctrines' (ⲛⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ), 'men of wickedness,' rival teachers, and law-bound communities. Editorial fatigue score moderate (+0.44) with polemic and hortatory rising in second half. Segments 19-25 form a polemical insertion identifying the cosmic Error with contemporary opponents; the substrate enumeration of five faculties resumes at seg 27.

segments.core_english: which Satan placed in the world {23} a multitude {24}
segments.temporal_note: Satan as cosmic agent placing things in the world — substrate dualistic action, not polemic against persons.
ⲛⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ (doctrines) and ⲛⲓⲣⲙ̄ⲃⲱⲛⲉϩ (men of wickedness) — explicit polemical identification of contemporary religious opponents under the rubric of 'evil fruit'.
'Bound in laws — laws which they hold together with their teacher' identifies contemporary law-based rival communities and their human teacher. Polemic against named opposing teachers/sects.
'Law of death' — extension of polemic against rival law-communities; their tasting/thirsting frames them as deluded.

segments.removed_material: Stripped polemical predication 'souls of death' which continues the polemic against opponents. Retained the cosmological 'this is the planting' which returns to substrate correspondential register (ⲡⲱϩⲛ).
segments.temporal_note: Pivot point — 'planting' brings the discourse back to cosmic register from polemic.

segments.removed_material: Stripped 'ⲡⲉⲧⲁ ⲡⲛ̄ⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ ⲁⲣⲁϩ' ('which the Lord named'). Citation formula attributing the good-fruit/evil-fruit dichotomy to 'the Lord' — this is later editorial dominical citation, importing the gospel parable.
segments.temporal_note: Citation formula 'the Lord named' is editorial — the parable of two trees enters via gospel citation, even though the underlying correspondence (good fruit/evil fruit) is ancient.
'Good fruit' continues correspondential register; here it is the cosmic predicate, not the gospel citation.
Structural break. 'Writings...all the doctrines are made manifest' — ⲛⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ as polemical category being exposed via writings. Editorial bridge to next exposition.
First-person teacher voice: 'I will set forth, I reveal to you, that you may...' — hortatory frame addressing audience directly. Editorial transition introducing the five-member exposition.

segments.core_english: {41} to {42} the evil. They have five members {43}
segments.temporal_note: Pentadic enumeration opener — 'They have five members' — classic substrate correspondential structure. Five-member counter-pentad parallels the five Sons/Worlds.

segments.core_coptic: ⲉⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧ{44} ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ ⲧⲥⲃⲱ ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ {45}

segments.core_english: {54} the bōlos, the final binding, the dispersing {55}
segments.temporal_note: Fifth pentad mapping: mind → ⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ (the eschatological lump/clod of darkness), final binding, dispersing. Pure substrate cosmological terminology — bōlos is a key Manichaean cosmological term but inherits older Iranian eschatological substrate.
Satan as cosmic agent (eschatological action) — substrate dualistic register; high polemic score is misleading because ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲁⲛⲁⲥ here is the cosmic Adversary, not a contemporary opponent.
